test_cases.description: Verifies that applying the new migration version executes DROP TABLE IF EXISTS for errata, adr_entries, and verification_results, and that those tables no longer exist in DuckDB afterward.
preconditions: A DuckDB database is initialised with the previous migration version applied (errata, adr_entries, and verification_results tables exist)
migrations.py contains the new migration version with DROP TABLE IF EXISTS statements
test_cases.input: Apply the new migration version via the migration runner against the populated DuckDB database.
test_cases.expected: All three DROP TABLE IF EXISTS statements complete without error; querying INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES returns no rows for errata, adr_entries, or verification_results.
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
apply_migration(db, new_version)
assert table_exists(db, 'errata') == False
assert table_exists(db, 'adr_entries') == False
assert table_exists(db, 'verification_results') == False

test_cases.description: Verifies that the new migration does not drop the session_summaries table and that it remains queryable after the migration.
preconditions: A DuckDB database is initialised with session_summaries table present and populated with at least one row
migrations.py new migration version is ready to apply
test_cases.input: Apply the new migration version via the migration runner.
test_cases.expected: session_summaries table still exists after migration; a SELECT query against it returns at least the pre-existing row(s) without error.
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
apply_migration(db, new_version)
assert table_exists(db, 'session_summaries') == True
rows = db.execute('SELECT * FROM session_summaries').fetchall()
assert len(rows) >= 1

test_cases.description: Verifies that the new migration is assigned a version number strictly greater than all existing migration versions and is recorded in the migration version table exactly once after application.
preconditions: A DuckDB database is initialised with all prior migration versions applied
The migration version table records existing version numbers
test_cases.input: Apply the new migration version via the migration runner.
test_cases.expected: The new migration version number is greater than all previously recorded versions; the migration version table contains exactly one record for the new version after application.
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
existing_versions = get_applied_migration_versions(db)
new_version = get_new_migration_version()
assert new_version > max(existing_versions)
apply_migration(db, new_version)
versions_after = get_applied_migration_versions(db)
assert versions_after.count(new_version) == 1

smoke_tests.description: Verifies that a coder session knowledge retrieval call uses only the three retained channels, produces a correctly structured context payload, and emits the simplified log line.
smoke_tests.trigger: A coder session calls retrieve() on a fox_provider instance with a DuckDB database containing review findings, cross-group reviews, and same-spec summaries.
mockable: logging handler for log line capture
expected_effects: retrieve() queries only review findings, cross-group reviews, and same-spec context summaries
cross_group_items contains only cross-review records, capped at max_cross_group_items
Log line matches 'Retrieved {N} review + {N} cross-group + {N} context items for {spec}'
Returned context payload contains no [ERRATA], [ADR], [VERIFY], [CROSS-GROUP] verdict, [CROSS-SPEC], or [PRIOR-RUN] tags

smoke_tests.description: Verifies that after all deletions and updates are applied, running the full pytest suite produces exit code 0 with no import errors or failures from deleted code.
smoke_tests.trigger: Developer executes pytest from the repository root after all code, test, and documentation changes have been applied.
expected_effects: pytest discovers no deleted test files (test_errata.py, test_adr.py, etc.)
No test file raises ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError at collection time
All remaining tests for review, cross-group review, and same-spec summary channels pass
No test output references a deleted module, function, or table
